questions.q: What heart rate is displayed on the monitor in this image?
questions.explain: The monitor visibly displays a heart rate of 88 beats per minute. This is within the usual resting adult range, although the clinical context still matters.
questions.alt: Photograph of an ECG monitor displaying a regular Lead III rhythm trace and a displayed heart rate of 88 beats per minute.
questions.credit: Image: medipics1066, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

questions.q: The displayed Lead III trace shows repeated QRS complexes at approximately equal intervals. Which description best fits this feature?
options: A pattern of frequent ventricular ectopics
questions.explain: The R waves appear at broadly equal intervals, supporting a regular rhythm. A single small monitor photograph is insufficient for a complete 12-lead ECG interpretation or definitive diagnosis.
questions.alt: Photograph of an ECG monitor displaying a regular Lead III rhythm trace and a displayed heart rate of 88 beats per minute.
